categories.main_business_segments: Ross Stores, Inc. operates two main off-price retail brands: Ross Dress for Less, the largest off-price apparel and home fashion chain in the U.S., and dd’s DISCOUNTS, which offers more moderately-priced merchandise. Both brands focus on selling first-quality, in-season, name brand and designer apparel, accessories, footwear, and home fashions for the entire family at significant discounts.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Ross leverages a highly automated distribution network and advanced information systems to support its off-price retail model. The company’s core operational methods include opportunistic purchasing, packaway inventory management, and frequent inventory turns, supported by centralized buying offices in major apparel markets and ongoing investments in supply chain and merchandising technology.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Ross targets value-conscious, middle-income households through its Ross Dress for Less stores, while dd’s DISCOUNTS serves customers from more moderate-income households. The company’s primary markets are consumers seeking branded, fashionable merchandise at substantial discounts compared to department and specialty stores.
categories.geographic_coverage: As of January 28, 2023, Ross operated 2,015 stores (1,693 Ross and 322 dd’s DISCOUNTS) across 40 states, the District of Columbia, and Guam. The company’s store footprint is concentrated in the United States, with significant presence in California, Texas, and Florida, and distribution centers strategically located to support regional operations.
categories.supply_chain_position: Ross operates at the downstream end of the supply chain as a retailer, purchasing merchandise directly from manufacturers and vendors, including excess inventory and closeouts. The company manages its own distribution centers and warehouses to support store replenishment and inventory management.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Ross’s strategic priorities include maintaining a strong value proposition through recognizable brands at deep discounts, expanding store count, investing in supply chain and information systems, and enhancing the in-store shopping experience. The company continues to focus on opportunistic buying, local market adaptation, and technology investments to support growth and operational efficiency.
categories.revenue_model: Ross generates revenue primarily through in-store sales of branded apparel, footwear, accessories, and home goods. The company does not operate an e-commerce platform, relying instead on its brick-and-mortar stores and a treasure-hunt shopping experience to drive sales.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Ross competes in the highly fragmented and competitive off-price retail sector against other off-price retailers (such as TJX Companies and Burlington), department stores, discount stores, specialty stores, warehouse clubs, and online retailers. Ross is positioned as the largest off-price apparel and home fashion chain in the U.S., emphasizing value and convenience.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2022, Ross reported $18.7 billion in sales, with a net income of $1.5 billion and 2,015 stores in operation. While sales declined 1.2% year-over-year due to inflationary pressures and changing consumer demand, the company has demonstrated long-term growth through consistent store expansion and strong cash flow generation.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Ross differentiates itself by offering a wide assortment of first-quality, in-season, branded merchandise at 20% to 60% (Ross) or 20% to 70% (dd’s DISCOUNTS) below regular department and specialty store prices. The company emphasizes a treasure-hunt, self-service shopping experience in organized, easy-to-shop stores, appealing to value-driven consumers seeking recognizable brands at compelling discounts.
